top_story_title: Juniper Session Smart Conductor command injection exploited in attacks, now KEV-listed with a 28 November due date
top_story_summary: CVE-2026-103406, an OS command injection in HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router, is being exploited in the wild. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 November 2026 with a remediation due date of 28 November 2026. Per CISA's description, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID.
top_actions: Inventory every Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router instance with its running version; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and the applicable mitigation.
Remove Conductor administrative and salt/minion communication paths from any internet-facing interface; restrict them to a dedicated management network or out-of-band segment.
Treat an internet-reachable Conductor as compromised: hunt for unexpected root processes, new local accounts, modified configuration templates and outbound connections before and after the upgrade.
After remediation, rotate Conductor admin credentials, API tokens, device certificates and any secrets held on the orchestrator - root access survives a patch otherwise.
Audit the configuration pushed to managed edge routers for unauthorized policy, service-route or tunnel changes made during the exposure window.
executive_summary: Exploited now: CVE-2026-103406, OS command injection as root in HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router, added to CISA KEV on 25 November 2026 with a 28 November due date.

Also exploited: Palo Alto Networks reports PHP2Shell and Fragnesia being chained against PAN-OS devices whose management interfaces are exposed to the internet. No CVE IDs or fixed builds stated in the reporting.

Five critical nginx vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123634) affect nginx 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, fixed upstream in 1.31.9 mainline and 1.30.7 stable. Cisco's product-impact advisory is still being updated.
Certificate trust work, not a patch: eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys are brute-forceable in seconds, and Cisco has published an emergency distrust advisory listing affected products.
Cisco UCS and UCS-based appliances carry a UEFI Secure Boot bypass reachable by an authenticated user account or anyone with physical access - relevant where UCS hosts network or security appliances.
One common control answers the two exploited stories: management planes off the internet, ACL'd to an out-of-band network, with MFA on every admin path.
key_actions: **Juniper** — Identify all Conductor and Session Smart Router instances and their running versions from asset inventory; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release or documented mitigation before scheduling the change.
**Juniper** — Patch or mitigate the orchestrator/controller before the edge devices, and validate certificate trust between Conductor and routers after the upgrade.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Determine immediately whether any PAN-OS management interface (web UI, SSH or XML/REST API) answers from the internet, and remove that exposure now rather than at the next change window.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Confirm the running PAN-OS version against the vendor's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first.
**Multiple** — Cross-reference the 10 newly listed CVEs against the asset inventory, filtered by model and running version, and record patched, mitigated or accepted risk against each device group.
**Multiple** — Prioritise CVE-2026-103406 on Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and apply mitigations per CISA's instruction.
**Cisco** — Subscribe to or re-check the Cisco advisory for the product list and fixed releases; do not assume a product is unaffected until it appears in Cisco's review as such.
**Cisco** — Meanwhile reduce exposure: take appliance web and management interfaces off the internet and ACL them to a management VLAN or out-of-band network.

headlines.title: Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-103406 in Juniper Session Smart Conductor is being exploited to execute arbitrary commands as root, and CISA has added it to the KEV catalog.

headlines.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks warns that attackers are chaining the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia flaws against PAN-OS devices with internet-exposed management interfaces.

headlines.title: Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
headlines.summary: CISA added 10 exploited flaws to the KEV catalog, among them root command injection in Juniper Session Smart gear and five Mitel MiCollab bugs, due 28 November 2026.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: Five critical nginx flaws that can lead to remote code execution affect nginx 1.9.5 through 1.31.8; Cisco is still assessing which of its products are impacted.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys can be brute-forced within seconds, and Cisco has issued an emergency distrust advisory naming the products that need action.

headlines.title: Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
headlines.summary: A UEFI Shell weakness lets an authenticated user, or anyone with physical access, bypass Secure Boot on Cisco UCS servers and UCS-based appliances and run unauthorized software.
